The `-p no:randomly` in the body's repro command is a silent no-op (pytest does not error on `-p no:<absent-plugin>`). **Correction 3 — the polluter set is ≥5 tests across ≥5 files adding 9 distinct keys, and the named file is not even the alphabetically-first one.** A registry-drift attribution probe over the 26 test files importing any fu3-registering module found drift from: `test_backend_poll.py` (`icl_prefix_impolite`, `wildchat_prefix_real545`), `test_issue1090_fu6.py` (`neg_sp_ph4`, `neg_sp_police`), `test_issue1090_fu7.py` (`icl_prefix_sycophancy`), `test_issue1586_read_organism.py` (`neg_default_assistant`, `neg_reph_curious`, `neg_wc_short`), `test_issue1947_resume_matrix.py` (`icl_prefix_writing_style`). So the body's fix sketch — add `try/finally` to the ONE `_wc_prefix()` helper — is necessary-but-insufficient whack-a-mole; the class regrows on the next dispatcher test.

**Root cause is a PRODUCTION seam, not the test helper.** `scripts/issue1090_fu3_worker.py:180` `ensure_context()` calls `register_fu3_contexts()` unconditionally, and `panel_name_for()` (line 196) registers filtered panels at runtime. Any test exercising a context-resolution seam mutates the process-global `CONTEXTS`. That registration is intentional production behavior — the defect is purely test cross-contamination, so the fix belongs in test hygiene (`tests/conftest.py`, which already carries the shared #1247 / #1265 / #1392 autouse guard family), NOT in the production seam.

**Open question the running probe resolves** (it decides the fixture's shape, so the plan waits on it): is the pollution IMPORT-time (module-level code at collection, before any test runs) or TEST-time (inside test bodies)? The first attribution pass was unreliable — it credited `test_backend_poll.py::test_poller_async_gcp_workload_crash_re_points_sidecar_and_emits_running`, but the minimal alphabetical pair `pytest -q tests/test_backend_poll.py tests/test_issue1090_fu3_dispatcher.py` PASSES (`198 passed`), which means the drift in the 26-file run came from another module's import during collection and was mis-attributed to the first test to tear down. This matters: a per-test snapshot-at-setup / restore-at-teardown fixture fixes TEST-time pollution but is INERT against import-time pollution (the snapshot would already contain it). A per-file `--collect-only` sweep in a fresh process per file is running now to attribute import-time drift exactly.
